newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish housing completions seen down again in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Polish housing completions seen down again in 1997.

text.p: Polish housing completions are expected to fall this year after a 18.2-percent slide in 1996, but the outlook for the sector is positive, the head of the Housing and Urban Development Office said.

Barbara Blida said on Thursday that despite the expected decline in 1997, the trend would soon reverse because of large-scale investment in the sector, new credit schemes and the continued fast pace of building starts.
"In 1997, the number of completed dwellings is likely to fall...but in 1998-99, we will start to see positive effects," Blida told a news conference. She gave no forecast figures.
According to the Central Statistical Office (GUS) some 54,850 dwellings were completed last year, down from 67,060 in 1995 and 74,970 in 1994.
Blida said new housing credit plans, like one launched late last year by state-owned bank Pekao SA, would speed up the pace of dwelling completions in several years.
Data released by the Housing and Urban Development Office showed investment in the construction sector increased by 27.2 percent in January-November 1996, up from a 21.3-percent rise in all of 1995.
Blida said at the end of 1996, some 580,000 dwellings were under construction against the country's estimated needs of 1.5 million new homes by the year 2000.

Blida said the government, which last year decided to keep preferential VAT rates on building and construction until 2000, would spend 150 million zlotys ($49.5 million) in housing subsidies this year, up from about 60 million in 1996.

Blida said the actual fall in dwelling completions may be smaller than GUS figures show because many families moved into individually built homes before they were finished. Those homes were not recorded as completed though they were inhabited.

"Individual builders, who finance construction partly by credit and partly by income, often move into their home before it is totally completed," she said. -- Wojciech Moskwa +48 22 653 9700 ($ = 3.031 Polish Zloty)
